observations:
Torah #6's bechina graph, despite having 68 edges and 82 nodes, resolves cleanly into 6 packages that align perfectly with the Torah's structural argument. The three-part Aleph structure (upper point / vav / lower point) provides a crystalline organizing principle that contains all positive bechinas: Package 1 (keter/upper point axis), Package 2 (lower point axis), Package 3 (vav/firmament axis), with Packages 4 and 5 capturing the two-directional spiritual expertise (ratzo/shuv = going up / coming down), and Package 6 as the single evil-domain cluster.

No new cross-Torah package category is required. The key structural observations:

1. The three-part Aleph (upper dot = keter/Moshe, vav = firmament/royal, lower dot = Yehoshua/moon) maps precisely to an existing conceptual framework in the dataset (sefirot, prophetic vision, letter shapes) — no new category needed.

2. The Ratzo-veShov (running-and-returning) dynamic in Packages 4 and 5 is a teaching-specific instance of the general upward/downward spiritual motion, not a new concept category. This same dynamic appears in other Torahs under different names.

3. The evil cluster (Package 6) is appropriately small — only 4 nodes — reflecting that Torah #6 is predominantly a positive teaching about teshuvah. The evil element (honor-seeking producing strife and divine withdrawal) is the foil to the positive path, not a developed evil system of its own.

4. The missing bechina edges noted in the additions file (אות כ"ף ↔ כתר, כתר ↔ המתנה, etc.) would, if added, strengthen Package 1 further without creating any new package. They belong to the existing keter cluster by nature.

5. The 'בקי' concept (expertise in both ratzo and shuv) that synthesizes Packages 4 and 5 is correctly placed in Package 1 (merged), since it represents the achieved state of the Way of teshuvah — the crown-level attainment that defines Package 1's dominant theme.
